ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $OD$ bisects $\angle AOB$, $OE$ bisects $\angle BOC$, $\angle COD=20^\circ$, $\angle AOB=140^\circ$. What is the measure of $\angle DOE$ in degrees?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $OE$ bisects $\angle BOC$,\\
it follows that $\angle COE = \frac{1}{2}\angle BOC = \frac{1}{2} \times 50^\circ = 25^\circ$,\\
therefore, $\angle DOE = \angle COE + \angle COD = 25^\circ + 20^\circ = \boxed{45^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, all rays emanate from point O, OA is horizontal to the left, and OB is to the upper right; inside ∠AOB, from OA to OB, OD, OC, and OE can be seen in order. Therefore the order of the rays around O is A-D-C-E-B, and C is located between D and B, and E is located between C and B. Reasoning: It is known that OD bisects ∠AOB, and ∠AOB=140°, so ∠DOB=140°÷2=70°. Also because C is between D and B, and ∠COD=20°, ∠BOC=∠DOB−∠DOC=70°−20°=50°. OE bisects ∠BOC, so ∠COE=50°÷2=25°. Finally, ∠DOE=∠DOC+∠COE=20°+25°=45°.
